title: kubectl, namespaces and contexts
summary: The six commands you use every day, and how to be sure which cluster you are talking to.

steps.title: The everyday verbs
body: kubectl get pods                      list (add -o wide for node + IP, -A for all namespaces)
kubectl describe pod shop-api-7d9f    details + Events: the first place to look when stuck
kubectl logs shop-api-7d9f            stdout/stderr of the container (-f follow, --previous)
kubectl exec -it shop-api-7d9f -- sh  a shell inside the running container
kubectl apply -f k8s/                 create or update from files
kubectl delete -f k8s/                remove what the files describe
Resource types have short names: `po` pods, `deploy` deployments, `svc` services, `ns` namespaces, `cm` configmaps. `kubectl get deploy,svc` lists two kinds at once.
`READY 0/1` means 0 of the pod's 1 containers are ready to serve.

steps.prompt: Match the question to the command that answers it.
pairs: Why is my pod stuck? (scheduler and kubelet messages)
What did the app print before it crashed?
Which node is each pod on?
Is the config file really inside the container?

steps.prompt: A container restarts every minute. `kubectl logs web-1` shows only the startup banner of the *new* attempt. How do you see the output of the attempt that crashed?
steps.explain: `--previous` (or `-p`) shows the logs of the last terminated container instance, which is usually where the stack trace is.

steps.title: Namespaces and contexts
body: A **namespace** is a folder inside one cluster: `dev`, `shop`, `monitoring`. Names must be unique only *within* a namespace, and RBAC and quotas are usually set per namespace. Without `-n`, kubectl uses `default` (or whatever your context says).
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=shop   # make shop the default
A **context** in `~/.kube/config` is a triple: *cluster + user + namespace*.
> **Tip:** Before any `delete` or `apply`, run `kubectl config current-context`. "I thought I was on dev" is the classic production outage. Many people show the context in their shell prompt.

steps.prompt: `kubectl get pods` shows nothing, but your teammate says the `shop-api` pods are running fine. What is the most likely reason?
options: You are looking at a different namespace (or context) than the one the pods are in
The pods are on a node you do not have access to
kubectl only shows pods you created
steps.explain: Try `kubectl get pods -A | grep shop-api` to find them, then add `-n <namespace>`.

steps.prompt: Complete the command that follows the logs of the `api` container in pod `shop-7f` in namespace `shop`.
steps.explain: `-c` picks a container when a pod has several; `-n` is the namespace.

steps.prompt: A pod's container exits with an error every time it starts, and Kubernetes waits longer and longer between restarts. Fill in the STATUS column exactly as `kubectl get pods` shows it.
steps.explain: *BackOff* means the kubelet is waiting (10s, 20s, 40s... up to 5 minutes) before the next restart. The cause is always in `kubectl logs --previous`.

steps.title: Read `kubectl get pods`
prompt: Write `List<string> NotReady(string output)` that takes the text of `kubectl get pods` (header line first) and returns the names of pods that are **not fully ready**: the two numbers in `READY` differ, or `STATUS` is not `Running` or `Completed`.
returns `["web-2"]`. A `Completed` pod shows `0/1` but is healthy (its work is done). Columns are separated by one or more spaces.
template:
var dojoOut = "NAME      READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
web-1     1/1     Running            0          2h
web-2     0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   5          10m
job-x     0/1     Completed          0          1h";
Dojo.Eq("example from the task", new List<string> { "web-2" }, NotReady(dojoOut));

var dojoOut2 = "NAME   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
a      1/2     Running   0          1m
b      0/1     Pending   0          1m
c      2/2     Running   1          1m
";
Dojo.Eq("running but 1/2 ready, and pending", new List<string> { "a", "b" }, NotReady(dojoOut2));
Dojo.Eq("header only", new List<string>(), NotReady("NAME   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE"));
hints: Skip the first line, then `Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)` each row.
Column 1 is `READY` like `1/2`: split on `/` and compare. Column 2 is `STATUS`.
